quick_ref.Theme: Nature Detective Academy — The Habitat Investigation

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Science CLIL Integration
content: Problem: Students often describe places using only basic adjectives (hot, cold, big) without comparing them scientifically.

Solution: We teach the biological concept of habitats alongside comparative grammar (-er than). Students learn to contrast extreme environments (hotter, colder, wetter) and explain why specific animals adapt to each condition.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the main habitats and basic comparatives. Focus on the mechanics of adding "-er than" to short adjectives.
Session 2: Explore how specific animals adapt to these environments. Practice making complex comparisons between animals and their habitats.
Session 3: Full production. Write a cohesive paragraph comparing two habitats and present it orally to the class.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show two habitat flashcards (e.g., desert and forest). The student must make a comparative sentence ("The desert is hotter than the forest.").
Communicative task (Step 5 - 10 min): The Habitat Match. Student A describes a habitat's climate using comparatives. Student B must guess the habitat and name an animal that lives there.

vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: DESERT has one S → DeSERT = deserted (empty). Don't confuse with deSSert!

vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: O-C-E-A-N: Only Cool Enormous Aquatic Nature

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): hotter than the forest / much hotter
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: HOT → HOTTER: double the T then add ER → the desert got HOTTER!

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): colder than the desert / much colder in winter
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: COLD + ER = just add ER → the Arctic just got COLDER!

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): tropical forest / animals in the forest
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: F-O-R-E-S-T: Find Our Rabbits Eating Sweet Things → animals eat in forests
RAIN + FOREST = a forest that RAINS all the time → most biodiverse habitat!
ARC + TIC = a frozen ARC → the Arctic is a giant icy curved region

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): adapt to the climate / adapt to their habitat
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: A + DAPT = One solution adopted → to adapt = find ONE way to survive
ENVIRON + MENT = to surround → your environment SURROUNDS you everywhere
WET + LAND = land that is always WET → home for frogs, crabs, and birds
GRASS + LAND = land covered in GRASS → lions roam African grasslands
CONDI + TION = the state (trạng thái) → conditions = the state of the environment

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): drier than the ocean / much drier
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: DRY → DRIER: drop Y, add IER → the desert is DRIER than the forest

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): deeper than the river / much deeper
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: DEEP + ER = just add ER → the ocean gets DEEPER as you swim down

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): wider than a lake / much wider
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: WIDE + R = add R to WIDE → the grassland is WIDER than the forest
COM + PARE = come in PAIRS → compare: A is ___er THAN B

vocab_tiers.Key Collocation(s): survive in the desert / survive harsh conditions
vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: SUR + VIVE = super + alive → survive = stay alive in tough places

Every animal needs a habitat — a place where it can find food, water, and shelter.
The Sahara Desert is the hottest and driest place on Earth.
Camels live there: they are bigger than sheep and can store more water than any other mammal.
The Amazon Rainforest is wetter and more biodiverse than any desert.
Tree frogs live there — they are smaller than toads but more colourful.
The Arctic is the coldest habitat.
Polar bears are the largest land predators and are better adapted to cold than any other bear.
Today, Max is presenting his science report about habitats.
"Hello! Today I will compare the polar region and the rainforest," he says.
"The polar region is covered in ice. It is much colder than the rainforest.
Polar bears live there safely. A polar bear is bigger than a monkey.
It has thick white fur to survive in the freezing snow.
The rainforest is a green jungle. It is hotter and wetter than the polar region.
Colorful birds and tiny insects live in the tall trees.
A parrot is smaller than a polar bear, but it can fly!
Both habitats are very important for the Earth.
Animals adapt perfectly to their homes.
Thank you for listening to my report!"

listening_script.text: Hello, geographers! Today we are learning about animal habitats. A habitat is the natural home of an animal. The desert is hotter than the forest. Camels live in the desert because it is dry. The ocean is colder than the desert. Fish live in the ocean because they need water. The Arctic is colder than any other habitat on Earth. Polar bears live there. Every animal's habitat is perfect for that animal. Listen and match each animal to its correct habitat on your worksheet!

Student A: State a fact ("The desert is hot!").
Student B: Make a comparison ("Yes, the desert is hotter than the forest!").

The desert is _______________ (hotter / colder / wetter) than the forest.
The rainforest is _______________ (wetter / drier / colder) than the desert.
The ocean is _______________ (bigger / smaller / hotter) than a river.
A polar bear is _______________ (colder / bigger / smaller) than a cat.
Animals _______________ (adapt / sleep / fly) to survive in nature.
A camel lives in the _______________ (desert / ocean / river).
The Arctic is _______________ (colder / hotter / wetter) than the jungle.
Fish live in a water _______________ (habitat / desert / tree).
A monkey is _______________ (smaller / bigger / hotter) than an elephant.
The _______________ (ocean / desert / sun) is full of saltwater.
